guidance: The catwalk starts at the spawn. Kickers beside the start deck put the catwalk's yellow rails right in front of the player; following them leads to the observation box and the beam (G3 p034 stat point, p031 sidebar).

The beam hangs over the busy middle. The tape is over the press and cooling tank, the zones every floor line crosses, so it is seen from below many times before it is reached (inferred from its position).

Pickups seed the hard route. A stat point at the balcony quarter pipe, another on the ductwork, and a deck on the balcony handrail give reasons to climb the back of the hall before the tape route is known (G3 p034–p035).

The guide's sidebar says it outright. "Bette Would Dig It" tells players to spend early stat points on Air, Hang Time and Speed for the tape (G3 p031): the first tape doubles as the stat-point tutorial.
Hidden on purpose: the observation box's link to the beam (a small ramp behind glass) and the platforms' link to the beam are only obvious once you stand on the upper layer.
designLogic: One tape, two ends. The tape sits mid-way along an upper loop; the back end needs meter, a sky and two leaps, the front end needs only exploration and a stop-and-ollie. The guide prints the hard way first and the easy way as a sidebar; the remake's guides print only the easy way (PS34, pcgamesn).

The easy end starts at the spawn. The catwalk kicker is one of the three choices the player faces at the start, so a curious first run can reach the observation box in about 11 s (G3 shot at 1:49) and the tape a few seconds later.
The hard end tests THPS3's air tools. Fill the Special Meter, sky off a banked wall into a grind, speed from a quarter pipe, leap, leap. It is the career's first lesson in "go up first, then across".
Above the main line, not beside it. The beam is over the press and the cooling tank, where the floor lines and two letters per group pass; the tape is visible from where it cannot be reached.
Pickups pre-teach the climb. Stat points and a deck on the balcony and ductwork reward the first visit to the upper layer (G3 p034–p035).
The tape needs no unlock. The level's two events (valves → core, bucket, press) are kept off the tape route, so the first tape tests movement only.
Letters stay on the floor. Every letter set tours the four floor zones; none touches the upper loop. The letters teach the floor lines, the tape teaches the second layer.
Failure costs a climb, not a run. A fall drops 6–9 m to the floor; the back door is ≈ 11 s from the spawn, so several attempts fit in two minutes. LP3's bail on the platform still reached the tape.
Expert shortcut by gap knowledge. The TAS reaches a platform from the back guardrail with a boneless over the molten tank (12 s from spawn). The level lets mastery skip the designed staircase.

The revert is the new link of the floor lines. All three of G3's lines join vert to manual with a revert (Wrap Around → revert → manual; stall → revert → manual; handplant → revert). The tape route itself does not need it.
Compact first level, vertical not wide. G3 calls the Foundry compact; its growth is in height (five layers), which prepares the much bigger Canada.
The remake scores the approach. COMBO letters on the back-door catwalk, cash on the tape's platform and a Hidden Deck on the rafters turn the easy route into a scored, populated line.
remakeChanges: Tape: same beam; remake guides give only the catwalk/glass-box route (PS34; pcgamesn)
Goal 'Cannonball Over the Half Pipe -or- 50-50 TC's Rail' -> 'Indy Over the Half Pipe'; High Combo 7,500; five pro goals
Three letter sets by skater group -> one set (≈ G1)
COMBO letters added on the back-door catwalk (pro goal)
New pickups: Cash ×3 (one beside the tape route), Hidden Deck on the rafters, Iron Galaxy logo at the top of the helix, Panda plushie, 2 stat points, 5 Forged Tonys (one on the ductwork)
PS1 edition (2001): different goals (Activate Press, Grind the Control Booth, Valves Unjammed); tape on the rafter gantry above the press; no core on the map
transfer: Mid-loop crystal. Build an upper loop of narrow platforms ≈ 6–8 m above the floor: catwalk from the spawn → small glass box → long beam (grindable platform edge, ≈ 0.4 m wide) → two hanging slabs → balcony. Put the crystal on the beam's midpoint, ≥ 7 m above any floor, over the level's busiest zone.

Two ends, two skill levels. Easy end: a kicker beside the spawn onto the catwalk, then a short ramp at the box that ollies straight into the beam grind (grind snap radius 2.1 m forgives the line-up). Hard end: a banked wall to wallride/vert-air up to the balcony, then two ollies across ≈ 6–8 m gaps (inside the ≈ 9.4 m cruise-ollie range) to a slab and to the beam.
Breakable box. Close the box with smashable glass (break-glass) so the easy end is visible but reads as "something to break into".
Seed the climb. Put two lesser pickups (or a trick-gate reward) on the balcony quarter pipe and on a high duct above the slabs, so the hard end is visited before the crystal route is known.
Keep walkers off. Hold the beam ≥ 7 m above the floor and ≥ 3 m from any ledge a walker can grab; the slabs and box are the only standable surfaces nearby, and both lie on the designed routes.
Cheap retries. Land a miss on flat floor beside the spawn-side catwalk kicker, so a retry is a ≈ 10–15 s climb inside the run.
openQuestions: Exact heights of the catwalk, balcony, platforms and beam: no source gives them; all are estimates.
Whether the tape is visible from the spawn deck: not seen in any frame I examined.
Where the glass box sits relative to the press: the PS1 map shows a glazed box above the press, the PS2 sources only say "glass-encased observation area" at the catwalk's end.
G3 announces 47 gaps but describes 44 plus the challenge; W Lil' Rail Hop repeats another gap's text.
The Neversoft Challenge "Nausea Grind!!!" is not located by the guide; the helix is a guess.
TAS3 Foundry glitches or GameCube-specific collision were not checked against the PS2 build.
The remake's tape pickup was not captured in LP34 (0:12:35–0:16:40 shows the catwalk and the Hidden Deck).
